The BookingAccess explicit-revoke-then-resave-same-session defect identified in this review (finding BA-01) should be fixed before the confirmed-booking read capability is relied upon for real users, since it currently causes a permanent per-tab lockout after a legitimate self-revoke.

findings.condition: A guest has saved confirmed-booking access (SaveBookingAccess issues a capability keyed by a client-generated requestId cached in sessionStorage under 'zao-booking-access-request:'+bookingId), then explicitly revokes that device's access via the ConfirmedBooking page's revoke button, and afterward returns to the same browser tab/session and clicks 'save' again for the same booking.
findings.impact: The client only mints a new crypto.randomUUID() requestId when sessionStorage has none yet (line 11: `if(!requestId){requestId=crypto.randomUUID();...}`), so after a revoke it resubmits the exact same (bookingId, requestId) pair to POST /api/booking-access/issue. In booking_access.issue (packages/db/migrations/0022_booking_access.sql, the 'IF FOUND THEN' branch checking `old.revoked_at IS NOT NULL`), the primary key (booking_id, request_id) still resolves to the now-revoked row, so the function unconditionally raises BOOKING_ACCESS_DENIED even though the guest still legitimately owns the confirmed booking and would otherwise qualify for a fresh capability. BookingAccess.issue() (packages/core/src/guest/booking-access.ts) catches this and rethrows a generic 401, and the UI shows a misleading '同じ要求を再照合してください...メール復旧接続待ちです' message implying an unresolved-response retry rather than a permanent per-session lockout. The only recovery is closing the tab (clearing sessionStorage); this is not covered by any Owner-disclosed gate and defeats the intended 'revoke, then re-save later' workflow implied by the revoke button's own label.
findings.evidence: apps/web/src/components/BookingAccess.tsx lines 9-13 (save()); packages/db/migrations/0022_booking_access.sql booking_access.issue() 'IF FOUND THEN ... old.revoked_at IS NOT NULL ... RAISE EXCEPTION BOOKING_ACCESS_DENIED'; packages/core/src/guest/booking-access.ts issue() catch block rethrowing generic BOOKING_ACCESS_DENIED/401. Neither tests/readiness/booking-access.ts nor tests/readiness/booking-access-ui.ts exercises revoke-then-resave with the same cached requestId; both only cover fresh issuance, exact-key response-loss replay, and rotation via distinct request keys.
findings.fix: Either (a) have the client detect an issue failure and mint/store a fresh requestId before allowing another save attempt for that booking (invalidate the cached sessionStorage entry on any /issue error, not just on success), or (b) change booking_access.issue so that a revoked row for the same (booking_id, request_id) is treated as 'not found' for reissue purposes (mint a new capability under a fresh key or update the same row) rather than being denied outright, provided the guest/booking ownership and lock checks still pass.
findings.test: Add a case to tests/readiness/booking-access-ui.ts: after issuing a capability and clicking the revoke button on the reservation page, navigate back to the guest booking confirmation view in the same browser context (same sessionStorage) and click 'save' again; assert the request succeeds and a new, usable capability is issued, instead of asserting/observing a permanent BOOKING_ACCESS_DENIED.
